blogs.preview:
If you send inventory to Amazon fulfillment centers, Amazon FBA prep is no longer optional background work, it is a core part of your inbound workflow.

As of January 1, 2026, Amazon ended in-house FBA prep and labeling services in the United States. Every unit must arrive fully prepped and scannable, or you risk delays, unplanned fees, or refused shipments.

This guide explains:
1. What FBA prep includes
2. Who must handle it
3. How requirements vary by product
4. How sellers typically manage prep at scale.

blogs.preview:
Launching a supplement brand on Amazon is not the same as launching a generic consumer product.

You are operating in a regulated category with two compliance layers:

1. U.S. dietary supplement rules (FDA)
2. Amazon’s marketplace policies, which are often stricter than the legal minimum.

If you skip either layer, you risk listing suppression, inbound rejections, or inventory disposal, not just a slow launch.

internal_linking_titles: The Ultimate Guide to Amazon FBA Prep
Wholesale/Private Label Prep for Amazon FBA & Walmart Fulfillment Services

blogs.preview:
Choosing the wrong barcode for an FBA shipment is one of the fastest ways to get inventory rejected at receiving.

The confusion is understandable, a UPC and an FNSKU can sit on the same product, serve different purposes, and, depending on your seller status, only one of them may actually be acceptable to Amazon.

A UPC identifies what a product is, while an FNSKU identifies which seller's inventory a specific unit belongs to inside Amazon's fulfillment network.

blogs.preview:
Sending expiration-dated inventory to Amazon FBA comes with rules that are stricter, and less forgiving, than most sellers expect.

Get the shelf life or label format wrong, and Amazon won't just flag the issue, it will dispose of the inventory, and that inventory generally isn't coming back.

Summary:
1. Amazon requires expiration-dated products to have more than 90 days of remaining shelf life when received at a fulfillment center.
2. Units within roughly 50 days of expiration are marked for disposal.

Walmart Fulfillment Services has its own prep and packaging rules, and while they overlap with Amazon FBA in some places, treating the two programs as interchangeable is a common way sellers end up with rejected shipments. One meaningful difference stands out immediately: Walmart still offers a paid prep service, something Amazon discontinued in the US at the start of 2026.

Summary:
Walmart WFS requires every item to:
1. Carry a GTIN or UPC barcode
2. Be packaged in a sealed, damage-resistant container
3. Meet specific palletizing and labeling standards before shipment

blogs.preview:
A single warehouse, one carrier contract, and one point of origin can work fine for years , until a flood, a port strike, or a system outage stops all of it at once. Brands that build in a backup 3PL aren't preparing for a hypothetical; they're preparing for the version of a disruption that eventually happens to almost every growing operation.

Summary:
Brands use a backup 3PL to avoid having their entire fulfillment operation depend on a single warehouse, carrier, or provider.

If the primary 3PL faces a disruption , a facility issue, a carrier problem, or a capacity crunch , the backup can absorb volume and keep orders moving instead of letting the business stall completely.

blogs.preview:
Summary:

1. TikTok Shop fulfillment is how orders placed in the app move from your inventory to the customer’s door, and in 2026, TikTok measures that performance strictly.

2. Brands must typically get regular orders scanned In Transit within 2 business days of Awaiting Shipment and Delivered within 6 business days, while maintaining metrics such as Late Dispatch Rate (LDR), On-Time Delivery Rate (OTDR), and Valid Tracking Rate (VTR).

3. You can fulfill through Fulfilled by TikTok (FBT), TikTok Shipping, or seller-controlled shipping (in-house or via a 3PL), depending on what your Seller Center account allows. This guide explains each path, the rules that trip up new sellers, and how to set up fulfillment without breaking multi-channel inventory.

blogs.meta_description: How ecommerce brands set up DTC fulfillment in 2026,in-house vs 3PL, costs, Shopify integration, multi-channel inventory, and evaluation checklist.
blogs.preview:
Summary

1. DTC fulfillment is the process of storing inventory, picking and packing website orders, shipping directly to consumers, and handling returns,without a retailer or marketplace sitting in the middle.

2. In 2026, most growing ecommerce brands eventually outsource some or all of this work to a 3PL when order volume, SKU complexity, or multi-channel sales (Shopify + TikTok + Amazon) exceed what an in-house team can ship accurately every day.

3. Setup success depends on three decisions: who fulfills (in-house, 3PL, or hybrid), how systems connect (real-time store-to-warehouse sync), and how inventory is allocated across channels so you do not oversell when one channel spikes.
